resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. pedagogy §26 line 48: harm: The judge's facts check out, but the harm does not survive and the proposed fix costs more than the defect.

Facts I verified:
- `module-2-start.md` appears only in prework L42 and L56, in eval and prototype copies, and in simulated-student result logs.
- No exercise, prompt or training body reads it.
- `name-your-challenge-1` asks three fresh interview questions and never opens the file.
- The `name-your-challenge` maintainer note says prework only "handed them the nudge".
- So no machine reader exists, and L48's "Module 2 builds ./challenge.md from these lines" overstates the mechanism.

Why it still fails:
1. **(a) Harm.** The file's reader is the student. The page frames it as a "three-line readiness note" "to leave yourself", costing 2 minutes (maintainer Time line), and L56 says "Bring to Module 2". It forces the student to pick a challenge, a source and a planning control before arriving. The student then carries those answers into the interview and into the "What challenge are you carrying" prompt in `building-agent-systems.md`. §26 targets reflection files that only prove reflection and have no reader. This is a pre-commitment note the student uses. A student who skips it loses nothing, because the interview runs fresh. The judge's "false consumer claim" is a loose human-mediated "builds", not a deception that leaves anyone worse off in the room.
2. **(c) Fix cost.**
   - Wiring `name-your-challenge-1` or `build-your-challenge-memory` to read the file is a prompt-body edit, so it needs a card. It also breaks the deliberate design that prework survives being skipped: the maintainer block says the Module 2 opener exists because students skip prework, and the prompt would need a conditional for an absent file.
   - Dropping the file write deletes a section Antti authored on 2026-08-24 (git blame on L40-42). It also breaks the L7 "readiness note" promise, the L56 "Bring to Module 2" callback and the 2-minute line in the Time budget.
3. **(g) Premise.** Whether students consult their own note in the room, or the trainer glances at it, is a maintainer-held fact about people. A repo grep cannot settle it, and silence in the repo is not evidence of no consumer (61a(g)).
4. **(e) Blame.** L48 was last rewritten by a compaction pass on 2026-11-01 (ab22d2471). That pass softened an earlier, stronger consumer claim. The file write was never new, and the §26 trigger is "before adding" such a write.

The finding should not stand as BLOCKING. At most it is a non-blocking wording nit on L48.
